**Strömsund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Strömsunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Straejmien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Strömsund](./Strömsund "Strömsund").

The nearest larger city is [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), the provincial capital of [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland"), which is located approximately 100 km to the south.

History
-------

Strömsund Municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of the former municipalities of Fjällsjö, Frostviken, Hammerdal and Ström. The most populous [locality](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden "Urban areas in Sweden") in the area, Strömsund, was chosen as administrative centre, and it also gave its name to the new entity.

Geography
---------

With an area of roughly 12,000 km2 (4,600 sq mi), it is the sixth largest in Sweden, and one of the most sparsely populated. The town Strömsund has a municipal population of about 3,500 and is located on the slopes of [Ströms vattudal](./Ströms_vattudal "Ströms vattudal"), the river that flows through the town. Among locals, the town itself is usually referred to as *Ström* or *Flata* (a reference to the flack slope on which the central parts of the town is built).

Economy
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Hallingsafall.JPG/250px-Hallingsafall.JPG)](./File:Hallingsafall.JPG)

[Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet").

[Forest industry](./Forestry "Forestry") has traditionally been an important industry, but today [tourism](./Tourism "Tourism") also has an important part. Like the rest of Jämtland, nature is what attracts visitors, with its blend of forests, mountains, lakes and rivers.

The two most visited sights are Hembygdsgården in Strömsund (16,000 visitors) and [Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet") (12,000 visitors).[[6]](./Strömsund_Municipality#cite_note-6)

Another popular site is the cave [Korallgrottan](./Korallgrottan "Korallgrottan").

[Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language \"Southern Sami language\"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden \"Municipalities of Sweden\") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County \"Jämtland County\") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden \"Sweden\"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre \"Administrative centre\") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.\\n\\nThe present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) \"Stad (Sweden)\") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.\\n\\nLocalities\\n----------\\n\\nThere are ten [localities](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden \"Urban areas in Sweden\") (or urban areas) in Östersund Municipality:[[3]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-3)\\n\\n| # | Locality | Population |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1 | **[Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\")** (part of) | 43,359 |\\n| 2 | [Brunflo](./Brunflo \"Brunflo\") | 3,916 |\\n| 3 | [Lit](./Lit,_Sweden \"Lit, Sweden\") | 1,051 |\\n| 4 | [Ope](./Ope \"Ope\") | 441 |\\n| 5 | [Tandsbyn](./Tandsbyn \"Tandsbyn\") | 396 |\\n| 6 | [Häggenås](./Häggenås \"Häggenås\") | 351 |\\n| 7 | [Orrviken](./Orrviken \"Orrviken\") | 239 |\\n| 8 | [Optand](./Optand \"Optand\") | 238 |\\n| 9 | [Marieby](./Marieby \"Marieby\") | 218 |\\n| 10 | [Fåker](./Fåker \"Fåker\") | 209 |\\n\\nThe municipal seat in [bold](./Emphasis_(typography) \"Emphasis (typography)\")\\n\\nPolitics and governance\\n-----------------------\\n\\nSwedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council \"Municipal council\") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) \"Municipal assembly (Sweden)\")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election \"General election\").\\n\\n### Political history\\n\\nÖstersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system \"Single-winner voting system\"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization \"Democratization\") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament \"Parliament\") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party \"Moderate Party\"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden \"Liberalism and centrism in Sweden\") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party \"Swedish Social Democratic Party\"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) \"Left Party (Sweden)\"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People\\'s party](./Liberal_People\\'s_Party_(Sweden) \"Liberal People\\'s Party (Sweden)\")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election \"1948 Swedish general election\"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund\\'s governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.\\n\\nA majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties \"Nordic agrarian parties\") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) \"Centre Party (Sweden)\") (previously known as *Peasant\\'s League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) \"Christian Democrats (Sweden)\") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare \"Swedish welfare\") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.\\n\\nThe first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation \"Centralisation\"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) \"Green Party (Sweden)\"). **Krokom Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Krokoms kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Krokomen tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Krokom](./Krokom "Krokom").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when the former municipalities of [Alsen](./Alsen,_Jämtland "Alsen, Jämtland"), [Föllinge](./Föllinge "Föllinge"), [Offerdal](./Offerdal "Offerdal") and [Rödön](./Rödön "Rödön") were amalgamated. The number of original local government entities in the area is nine, and amalgamations had also taken place in 1952 and 1969.

**Krokom Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Krokoms kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Krokomen tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Krokom](./Krokom "Krokom").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when the former municipalities of [Alsen](./Alsen,_Jämtland "Alsen, Jämtland"), [Föllinge](./Föllinge "Föllinge"), [Offerdal](./Offerdal "Offerdal") and [Rödön](./Rödön "Rödön") were amalgamated. The number of original local government entities in the area is nine, and amalgamations had also taken place in 1952 and 1969.

**Bräcke Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bräcke kommun*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 when "old" Bräcke Municipality was amalgamated with Kälarne and Revsund. The three former municipalities had been created in 1952. The number of original entities (as of 1863) were six. Due to the declining population in the area further amalgamations have been proposed, but rejected.

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

**Åre Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Åre kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Ååren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Järpen](./Järpen "Järpen").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of "old" Åre Municipality with the surrounding municipalities Hallen, Kall, Mörsil and Undersåker. The largest village, Järpen, situated in Undersåker, was chosen as the seat of the new entity.

**Berg Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bergs kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Bïerjien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Svenstavik](./Svenstavik "Svenstavik").

The present municipality was formed in 1971 when "old" Berg Municipality was amalgamated with four other entities.

As often in northern Sweden the municipality is one of the larger in terms of area, but one of the smaller in terms of population.

Geography
---------

The [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") [Hoverberget](./Hoverberget "Hoverberget") lies within Berg Municipality, near Svenstavik. The high mountain [Helags](./Helags "Helags") and Sweden's highest public road, over Flatruet, are located in the western end of Berg Municipality. Berg means mountain in Swedish, and the name of the municipality (and the Berg Parish) comes from Hoverberget.

**Ragunda Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Ragunda kommun*; [[ˈrɑ̂ːˌɡɵnːda]](./Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish"))[[3]](./Ragunda_Municipality#cite_note-3) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is in [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand "Hammarstrand").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when "old" Ragunda Municipality was amalgamated with the municipalities of Fors and Stugun. Further amalgamations have been discussed due to declining population but have not been carried out.

Ragunda Municipality is known for being the site of the [King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building](./King_Chulalongkorn_Memorial_Building "King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building"), which is by the village Utanede. Designed as a [Thai](./Thailand "Thailand") royal [pavilion](./Pavilion "Pavilion"), the only one of its kind outside Thailand, it was raised in 1997 in commemoration of King [Chulalongkorn](./Chulalongkorn "Chulalongkorn")'s visit there a century earlier.

[Döda fallet](./Döda_fallet "Döda fallet") (*The dead waterfall*) is an extinct [whitewater](./Whitewater "Whitewater") [rapid](./Rapids "Rapids") in a [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") and one of the major tourist attractions of the municipality.

**Strömsund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Strömsunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Straejmien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Strömsund](./Strömsund "Strömsund").

The nearest larger city is [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), the provincial capital of [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland"), which is located approximately 100 km to the south.

History
-------

Strömsund Municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of the former municipalities of Fjällsjö, Frostviken, Hammerdal and Ström. The most populous [locality](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden "Urban areas in Sweden") in the area, Strömsund, was chosen as administrative centre, and it also gave its name to the new entity.

Geography
---------

With an area of roughly 12,000 km2 (4,600 sq mi), it is the sixth largest in Sweden, and one of the most sparsely populated. The town Strömsund has a municipal population of about 3,500 and is located on the slopes of [Ströms vattudal](./Ströms_vattudal "Ströms vattudal"), the river that flows through the town. Among locals, the town itself is usually referred to as *Ström* or *Flata* (a reference to the flack slope on which the central parts of the town is built).

Economy
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Hallingsafall.JPG/250px-Hallingsafall.JPG)](./File:Hallingsafall.JPG)

[Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet").

[Forest industry](./Forestry "Forestry") has traditionally been an important industry, but today [tourism](./Tourism "Tourism") also has an important part. Like the rest of Jämtland, nature is what attracts visitors, with its blend of forests, mountains, lakes and rivers.

The two most visited sights are Hembygdsgården in Strömsund (16,000 visitors) and [Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet") (12,000 visitors).[[6]](./Strömsund_Municipality#cite_note-6)

Another popular site is the cave [Korallgrottan](./Korallgrottan "Korallgrottan").

**Krokom Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Krokoms kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Krokomen tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Krokom](./Krokom "Krokom").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when the former municipalities of [Alsen](./Alsen,_Jämtland "Alsen, Jämtland"), [Föllinge](./Föllinge "Föllinge"), [Offerdal](./Offerdal "Offerdal") and [Rödön](./Rödön "Rödön") were amalgamated. The number of original local government entities in the area is nine, and amalgamations had also taken place in 1952 and 1969.

You are a Web Agent, that is designed to manage and complete TASKs in iterative CYCLES based on input from the USER through Web protocols in the Web ENVIRONMENT.

TASK Definition
- A TASK is an instruction of the USER to achieve a specified purpose.
- A TASK requires multiple CYCLES to complete.
- Complete the TASK by only using the available TOOLS.

CYCLES Definition
- A CYCLE is specified through a Thought-Act-Observe pattern.
- 1) Thought: Carefully analyze the TASK and the descriptions in the representations gathered through the USER and previously observed information. Evaluate the completion status of the TASK.
- 2) Act: Formulate a plan with ACTIONS that directly contribute to completing the TASK, potentially across multiple CYCLES. Do NEVER expand beyond the original TASK boundaries.
- 3) Observe: The USER and the ENVIRONMENT can provide observations that help to refine the plan.

LOOP Definition
- A LOOP is a sequence of CYCLES that is used to finish a TASK.
- Once the LOOP is finished you MUST call `final_answer` to report the result.

TOOLS
- A TOOL is an operation that allows you to percieve or interact with the ENVIRONMENT.
- During each CYCLE, invoke one or multiple TOOLS.
- The following TOOLS are available to you:

- **get**: Fetches a URL and returns the resource content. Takes a URL as input and returns the the URL with the resource content.

  - Inputs:

- **put**: Sends a PUT request to a URL. Use for replacing or updating resources. Takes URL and text_body as input; sends the body with Content-Type: text/plain.
  - Inputs:
  
    - `_rationale` (string): Describe your reasoning step-by-step in plain text BEFORE calling any tool.

- **final_answer**: Call this when you are done with the task. Provide the list of URLs that answer the user's question and the task state (completed, partial, failed, or unclear).

ENVIRONMENT
* Follow links via `get()` and submit forms via `post()` judiciously.
* Only use URIs previously mentioned in or discovered from representations.
* Do not use your general knowledge to guess, generate or construct URIs.

FINISHING

**Bräcke Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bräcke kommun*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 when "old" Bräcke Municipality was amalgamated with Kälarne and Revsund. The three former municipalities had been created in 1952. The number of original entities (as of 1863) were six. Due to the declining population in the area further amalgamations have been proposed, but rejected.

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

------------

This is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality's electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television "Swedish Television")'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån "Statistiska Centralbyrån") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)

Residents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.

In total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Indicators are in percentage points except population totals and income.

**Åre Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Åre kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Ååren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Järpen](./Järpen "Järpen").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of "old" Åre Municipality with the surrounding municipalities Hallen, Kall, Mörsil and Undersåker. The largest village, Järpen, situated in Undersåker, was chosen as the seat of the new entity.

**Berg Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bergs kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Bïerjien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Svenstavik](./Svenstavik "Svenstavik").

The present municipality was formed in 1971 when "old" Berg Municipality was amalgamated with four other entities.

As often in northern Sweden the municipality is one of the larger in terms of area, but one of the smaller in terms of population.

Geography
---------

The [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") [Hoverberget](./Hoverberget "Hoverberget") lies within Berg Municipality, near Svenstavik. The high mountain [Helags](./Helags "Helags") and Sweden's highest public road, over Flatruet, are located in the western end of Berg Municipality. Berg means mountain in Swedish, and the name of the municipality (and the Berg Parish) comes from Hoverberget.

**Ragunda Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Ragunda kommun*; [[ˈrɑ̂ːˌɡɵnːda]](./Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish"))[[3]](./Ragunda_Municipality#cite_note-3) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is in [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand "Hammarstrand").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when "old" Ragunda Municipality was amalgamated with the municipalities of Fors and Stugun. Further amalgamations have been discussed due to declining population but have not been carried out.

Ragunda Municipality is known for being the site of the [King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building](./King_Chulalongkorn_Memorial_Building "King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building"), which is by the village Utanede. Designed as a [Thai](./Thailand "Thailand") royal [pavilion](./Pavilion "Pavilion"), the only one of its kind outside Thailand, it was raised in 1997 in commemoration of King [Chulalongkorn](./Chulalongkorn "Chulalongkorn")'s visit there a century earlier.

[Döda fallet](./Döda_fallet "Döda fallet") (*The dead waterfall*) is an extinct [whitewater](./Whitewater "Whitewater") [rapid](./Rapids "Rapids") in a [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") and one of the major tourist attractions of the municipality.

**Strömsund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Strömsunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Straejmien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Strömsund](./Strömsund "Strömsund").

The nearest larger city is [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), the provincial capital of [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland"), which is located approximately 100 km to the south.

History
-------

Strömsund Municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of the former municipalities of Fjällsjö, Frostviken, Hammerdal and Ström. The most populous [locality](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden "Urban areas in Sweden") in the area, Strömsund, was chosen as administrative centre, and it also gave its name to the new entity.

Geography
---------

With an area of roughly 12,000 km2 (4,600 sq mi), it is the sixth largest in Sweden, and one of the most sparsely populated. The town Strömsund has a municipal population of about 3,500 and is located on the slopes of [Ströms vattudal](./Ströms_vattudal "Ströms vattudal"), the river that flows through the town. Among locals, the town itself is usually referred to as *Ström* or *Flata* (a reference to the flack slope on which the central parts of the town is built).

Economy
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Hallingsafall.JPG/250px-Hallingsafall.JPG)](./File:Hallingsafall.JPG)

[Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet").

[Forest industry](./Forestry "Forestry") has traditionally been an important industry, but today [tourism](./Tourism "Tourism") also has an important part. Like the rest of Jämtland, nature is what attracts visitors, with its blend of forests, mountains, lakes and rivers.

The two most visited sights are Hembygdsgården in Strömsund (16,000 visitors) and [Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet") (12,000 visitors).[[6]](./Strömsund_Municipality#cite_note-6)

Another popular site is the cave [Korallgrottan](./Korallgrottan "Korallgrottan").

**Krokom Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Krokoms kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Krokomen tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Krokom](./Krokom "Krokom").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when the former municipalities of [Alsen](./Alsen,_Jämtland "Alsen, Jämtland"), [Föllinge](./Föllinge "Föllinge"), [Offerdal](./Offerdal "Offerdal") and [Rödön](./Rödön "Rödön") were amalgamated. The number of original local government entities in the area is nine, and amalgamations had also taken place in 1952 and 1969.

[Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language \"Southern Sami language\"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden \"Municipalities of Sweden\") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County \"Jämtland County\") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden \"Sweden\"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre \"Administrative centre\") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.\\n\\nThe present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) \"Stad (Sweden)\") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.\\n\\nLocalities\\n----------\\n\\nThere are ten [localities](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden \"Urban areas in Sweden\") (or urban areas) in Östersund Municipality:[[3]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-3)\\n\\n| # | Locality | Population |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1 | **[Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\")** (part of) | 43,359 |\\n| 2 | [Brunflo](./Brunflo \"Brunflo\") | 3,916 |\\n| 3 | [Lit](./Lit,_Sweden \"Lit, Sweden\") | 1,051 |\\n| 4 | [Ope](./Ope \"Ope\") | 441 |\\n| 5 | [Tandsbyn](./Tandsbyn \"Tandsbyn\") | 396 |\\n| 6 | [Häggenås](./Häggenås \"Häggenås\") | 351 |\\n| 7 | [Orrviken](./Orrviken \"Orrviken\") | 239 |\\n| 8 | [Optand](./Optand \"Optand\") | 238 |\\n| 9 | [Marieby](./Marieby \"Marieby\") | 218 |\\n| 10 | [Fåker](./Fåker \"Fåker\") | 209 |\\n\\nThe municipal seat in [bold](./Emphasis_(typography) \"Emphasis (typography)\")\\n\\nPolitics and governance\\n-----------------------\\n\\nSwedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council \"Municipal council\") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) \"Municipal assembly (Sweden)\")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election \"General election\").\\n\\n### Political history\\n\\nÖstersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system \"Single-winner voting system\"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization \"Democratization\") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament \"Parliament\") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party \"Moderate Party\"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden \"Liberalism and centrism in Sweden\") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party \"Swedish Social Democratic Party\"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) \"Left Party (Sweden)\"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People\\'s party](./Liberal_People\\'s_Party_(Sweden) \"Liberal People\\'s Party (Sweden)\")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election \"1948 Swedish general election\"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund\\'s governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.\\n\\nA majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties \"Nordic agrarian parties\") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) \"Centre Party (Sweden)\") (previously known as *Peasant\\'s League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) \"Christian Democrats (Sweden)\") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare \"Swedish welfare\") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.\\n\\nThe first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation \"Centralisation\"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) \"Green Party (Sweden)\"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.\\n\\nDemographics\\n------------\\n\\nThis is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality\\'s electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election \"2022 Swedish general election\") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television \"Swedish Television\")\\'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån \"Statistiska Centralbyrån\") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)\\n\\nResidents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor \"Swedish kronor\"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.\\n\\nIn total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Its [seat](./Administrative_centre \"Administrative centre\") is located in [Strömsund](./Strömsund \"Strömsund\").\\n\\nThe nearest larger city is [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), the provincial capital of [Jämtland](./Jämtland \"Jämtland\"), which is located approximately 100\\xa0km to the south.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\nStrömsund Municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of the former municipalities of Fjällsjö, Frostviken, Hammerdal and Ström. The most populous [locality](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden \"Urban areas in Sweden\") in the area, Strömsund, was chosen as administrative centre, and it also gave its name to the new entity.\\n\\nGeography\\n---------\\n\\nWith an area of roughly 12,000\\xa0km2 (4,600\\xa0sq\\xa0mi), it is the sixth largest in Sweden, and one of the most sparsely populated. The town Strömsund has a municipal population of about 3,500 and is located on the slopes of [Ströms vattudal](./Ströms_vattudal \"Ströms vattudal\"), the river that flows through the town. Among locals, the town itself is usually referred to as *Ström* or *Flata* (a reference to the flack slope on which the central parts of the town is built).\\n\\n### Localities\\n\\nThere are seven [localities](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden \"Urban areas in Sweden\") (or urban areas) in Strömsund Municipality:[[3]](./Strömsund_Municipality#cite_note-3)\\n\\n| # **Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

Demographics
------------

This is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality's electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television "Swedish Television")'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån "Statistiska Centralbyrån") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)

Residents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.

In total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Indicators are in percentage points except population totals and income.

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

Demographics
------------

This is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality's electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television "Swedish Television")'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån "Statistiska Centralbyrån") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)

Residents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.

In total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Indicators are in percentage points except population totals and income.

**Bräcke Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bräcke kommun*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 when "old" Bräcke Municipality was amalgamated with Kälarne and Revsund. The three former municipalities had been created in 1952. The number of original entities (as of 1863) were six. Due to the declining population in the area further amalgamations have been proposed, but rejected.

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

------------

This is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality's electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television "Swedish Television")'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån "Statistiska Centralbyrån") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)

Residents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.

In total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Indicators are in percentage points except population totals and income.

**Åre Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Åre kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Ååren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Järpen](./Järpen "Järpen").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of "old" Åre Municipality with the surrounding municipalities Hallen, Kall, Mörsil and Undersåker. The largest village, Järpen, situated in Undersåker, was chosen as the seat of the new entity.

**Berg Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bergs kommun*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Bïerjien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Svenstavik](./Svenstavik "Svenstavik").

The present municipality was formed in 1971 when "old" Berg Municipality was amalgamated with four other entities.

As often in northern Sweden the municipality is one of the larger in terms of area, but one of the smaller in terms of population.

Geography
---------

The [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") [Hoverberget](./Hoverberget "Hoverberget") lies within Berg Municipality, near Svenstavik. The high mountain [Helags](./Helags "Helags") and Sweden's highest public road, over Flatruet, are located in the western end of Berg Municipality. Berg means mountain in Swedish, and the name of the municipality (and the Berg Parish) comes from Hoverberget.

**Ragunda Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Ragunda kommun*; [[ˈrɑ̂ːˌɡɵnːda]](./Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish"))[[3]](./Ragunda_Municipality#cite_note-3) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is in [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand "Hammarstrand").

The present municipality was formed in 1974, when "old" Ragunda Municipality was amalgamated with the municipalities of Fors and Stugun. Further amalgamations have been discussed due to declining population but have not been carried out.

Ragunda Municipality is known for being the site of the [King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building](./King_Chulalongkorn_Memorial_Building "King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building"), which is by the village Utanede. Designed as a [Thai](./Thailand "Thailand") royal [pavilion](./Pavilion "Pavilion"), the only one of its kind outside Thailand, it was raised in 1997 in commemoration of King [Chulalongkorn](./Chulalongkorn "Chulalongkorn")'s visit there a century earlier.

[Döda fallet](./Döda_fallet "Döda fallet") (*The dead waterfall*) is an extinct [whitewater](./Whitewater "Whitewater") [rapid](./Rapids "Rapids") in a [nature reserve](./Nature_reserve "Nature reserve") and one of the major tourist attractions of the municipality.

**Strömsund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Strömsunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Straejmien tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Strömsund](./Strömsund "Strömsund").

The nearest larger city is [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), the provincial capital of [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland"), which is located approximately 100 km to the south.

History
-------

Strömsund Municipality was formed in 1974 through the amalgamation of the former municipalities of Fjällsjö, Frostviken, Hammerdal and Ström. The most populous [locality](./Urban_areas_in_Sweden "Urban areas in Sweden") in the area, Strömsund, was chosen as administrative centre, and it also gave its name to the new entity.

Geography
---------

With an area of roughly 12,000 km2 (4,600 sq mi), it is the sixth largest in Sweden, and one of the most sparsely populated. The town Strömsund has a municipal population of about 3,500 and is located on the slopes of [Ströms vattudal](./Ströms_vattudal "Ströms vattudal"), the river that flows through the town. Among locals, the town itself is usually referred to as *Ström* or *Flata* (a reference to the flack slope on which the central parts of the town is built).

Economy
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Hallingsafall.JPG/250px-Hallingsafall.JPG)](./File:Hallingsafall.JPG)

[Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet").

[Forest industry](./Forestry "Forestry") has traditionally been an important industry, but today [tourism](./Tourism "Tourism") also has an important part. Like the rest of Jämtland, nature is what attracts visitors, with its blend of forests, mountains, lakes and rivers.

The two most visited sights are Hembygdsgården in Strömsund (16,000 visitors) and [Hällingsåfallet](./Hällingsåfallet "Hällingsåfallet") (12,000 visitors).[[6]](./Strömsund_Municipality#cite_note-6)

Another popular site is the cave [Korallgrottan](./Korallgrottan "Korallgrottan").

The number of original local government entities in the area is nine, and amalgamations had also taken place in 1952 and 1969.

**Östersund Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Östersunds kommun*; [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Staaren tjïelte*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), which is also the county seat of Jämtland County.

The present municipality was formed in 1971 by the amalgamation of the [City](./Stad_(Sweden) "Stad (Sweden)") of Östersund with five surrounding rural municipalities.

Politics and governance
-----------------------

Swedish municipalities are responsible for government-mandated duties, and elections for the [municipal council](./Municipal_council "Municipal council") (*[kommunfullmäktige](./Municipal_assembly_(Sweden) "Municipal assembly (Sweden)")*) are held every four years, parallel to the [general elections](./General_election "General election").

### Political history

Östersund gained a city council (*stadsfullmäktige*) in 1863, known as *Östersunds stad*, and each member was elected through a [single-winner voting system](./Single-winner_voting_system "Single-winner voting system"). Sweden was [democratized](./Democratization "Democratization") in the end of the 1910s and a more [parliamentarian](./Parliament "Parliament") election system was introduced. Östersund continued to be governed by the *burghers*, unlike Sweden nationally. The dominating parties were [the conservatives](./Moderate_Party "Moderate Party"), [the freeminded](./Liberalism_and_centrism_in_Sweden "Liberalism and centrism in Sweden") and the [social democrats](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party"). The latter did become the single largest party in 1938 but due to a strong centre-right majority it remained in opposition. The only other party present in Östersund was [the communists](./Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)"), though they had little support in the city, having entered the city council in 1922 and lost representation completely in 1930. The conservatives was by far the largest party and had a majority of its own with 18 seats in 1922. After the municipal elections of 1950 the situation had changed. The conservatives was the smallest party with 10 seats, the liberals (now represented by [the Liberal People's party](./Liberal_People's_Party_(Sweden) "Liberal People's Party (Sweden)")) had 11 and the social democrats 19. This was in contrast to the turnout on a national level, where the social democrats had been the dominant party for over a decade gaining e.g. 46 percent of the votes in the [general elections of 1948](./1948_Swedish_general_election "1948 Swedish general election"). In 1952 a social democrat was appointed chairman of Östersund's governing body, due to the lack of political blocs and the strive for mutual agreements.

A majority for the social democrats was achieved first in 1962. The political scene was shortly afterwards altered, in 1966, when the [agrian and rural](./Nordic_agrarian_parties "Nordic agrarian parties") [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)") (previously known as *Peasant's League*) got into the city council, after broadening its scope to include non-farmers, alongside the [Christian Democrats](./Christian_Democrats_(Sweden) "Christian Democrats (Sweden)") (though not present on the national political scene) and the communists returning after a 40-year period of absence. *The burghers* was thus back in power. Following the rise of [Swedish welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare") the small municipalities could not cope with their assigned duties. As a result, large municipality blocks were introduced and *Östersunds stad* was heavily enlarged and several districts kilometres away from the city were included in the new *Östersund Municipality*.

The first election for the new municipality was held in 1970 and it was a large success for the Centre Party, both locally in Östersund and nationally due to its opposition towards [centralisation](./Centralisation "Centralisation"). Having entered in 1966 with 4 seats it now possessed one fourth of the total number of seats (which was mainly due to support from the city, not the newly included rural areas). Block politics formation became prominent and the Centre Party became the leading party for the centre-right block, whilst the Social Democrats came to dominate the left block. The Social Democrats regained power in 1980 and has since governed Östersund Municipality until present day (excluding a brief period in the 1990s) supported by the communists (after 1991 known as the Left Party) and occasionally the [Green Party](./Green_Party_(Sweden) "Green Party (Sweden)"). The Green Party has been in the municipal council since 1982.

Demographics
------------

This is a demographic table based on Östersund Municipality's electoral districts in the [2022 Swedish general election](./2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election") sourced from [SVT](./Swedish_Television "Swedish Television")'s election platform, in turn taken from [SCB](./Statistiska_Centralbyrån "Statistiska Centralbyrån") official statistics.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4)

Residents include everyone registered as living in the district, regardless of age or citizenship status. Valid voters indicate Swedish citizens above the age of 18 who therefore can vote in general elections. Left vote and right vote indicate the result between the two major blocs in said district in the 2022 general election. Employment indicates the share of people between the ages of 20 and 64 who are working taxpayers. Foreign background is defined as residents either born abroad or with two parents born outside of Sweden. Median income is the received monthly income through either employment, capital gains or social grants for the median adult above 20, also including pensioners in [Swedish kronor](./Swedish_kronor "Swedish kronor"). The section about college graduates indicates any degree accumulated after high school.

In total there were 49,635 Swedish citizens of voting age resident in the municipality.[[4]](./Östersund_Municipality#cite_note-ÖstersundVal2022-4) 58.5% voted for the left coalition and 40.2% for the right coalition. Indicators are in percentage points except population totals and income.

**Bräcke Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bräcke kommun*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 when "old" Bräcke Municipality was amalgamated with Kälarne and Revsund. The three former municipalities had been created in 1952. The number of original entities (as of 1863) were six. Due to the declining population in the area further amalgamations have been proposed, but rejected.
